prompt: What does `pl render` do?

choices.text: Fills the holes and prints the prompt
choices.why: Right: the cheapest test there is.

choices.text: Calls the model once and prints the reply
choices.why: That is `pl run` followed by `pl show`.

choices.text: Checks a reply against the five checks
choices.why: That is `pl check`.

choices.text: Formats a run file as a table for a person to read
choices.why: Nothing in `pl` does that; `pl show` prints one reply.

prompt: `pl render` was given no value for `{{language}}`. With what exit status did it stop?
hint: The last line of the transcript.

prompt: Why keep one reply template with `{{shop}}` and `{{language}}` rather than a copy of the prompt for each shop and language?
hint: Where does the next fix go?

choices.text: Copies are slower for the model to read
choices.why: The model reads one rendered prompt either way.

choices.text: An instruction then lives in one file, so a fix is made once
choices.why: Right: two copies are two places to fix, and one gets forgotten.

choices.text: A template makes the model follow its instructions more closely than a copy would
choices.why: Both replies promised a refund the template forbids.

choices.text: Ollama only accepts prompts that contain placeholders
choices.why: Ollama receives the rendered text and knows nothing of placeholders.

prompt: When `pl run` calls the model, what does the model read?

choices.text: The template, placeholders and all
choices.why: The placeholders are filled before the call.

choices.text: The template once, then each message separately
choices.why: Each call carries the whole filled prompt.

choices.text: The prompt the template becomes once its holes are filled
choices.why: Right: what `pl render` prints.

choices.text: Only the message, with the instructions cached by the harness
choices.why: Nothing is cached; the instructions go with every call.

prompt: Both replies to `t01`, in English and in Portuguese, promised a refund, and `reply.txt` says not to. What does that show about templates?

choices.text: That the Portuguese translation of the rule was wrong
choices.why: The rule is written once, in English; only the language value changed.

choices.text: It keeps the rule in one place; obeying it is another matter
choices.why: Right: obeying is measured, lesson 12.

choices.text: That `{{language}}` was filled in the wrong place
choices.why: Both replies came back in the right language.

choices.text: That the rule must be repeated in every language the shop writes in
choices.why: Repeating a rule is lesson 2's mistake; the fix is to measure it.

prompt: By default, what does Jinja2 render in place of an undefined variable?

choices.text: The placeholder exactly as written
choices.why: That is Python's `string.Template` with `safe_substitute`.

choices.text: An error, and nothing is rendered
choices.why: That is what `pl render` does, not Jinja2 by default.

choices.text: An empty string
choices.why: Right, which is why nothing shows up as an error.

choices.text: The word `undefined`
choices.why: Jinja2's default undefined renders as an empty string.

prompt: Why must a missing value stop the run rather than render as empty?
hint: What can tell an empty hole from a short sentence?

choices.text: Because the model refuses a prompt with an empty hole
choices.why: The model gets a sentence and guesses around it.

choices.text: Nothing later tells an empty hole from a short sentence
choices.why: Right: the defect would stay in place silently.

choices.text: Because an empty value costs more tokens
choices.why: An empty value costs fewer tokens, if anything.

choices.text: Because `pl check` cannot parse replies to a broken prompt
choices.why: It parses whatever comes back.

prompt: Somebody runs the reply template with `--var tone=warm`, and the template has no `{{tone}}`. What happened?

choices.text: The replies came back warmer, as asked
choices.why: The value never reached the model.

choices.text: The run stopped with an error
choices.why: An unused value is a warning; the run went ahead.

choices.text: The value reached nothing, with a warning per case
choices.why: Right: three warnings for three messages.

choices.text: The value was appended to the end of the prompt
choices.why: `render()` only fills the holes the template has.

prompt: Why render one case before running a template you have just changed?
hint: What does a run of forty do with the warning?

choices.text: Because `pl run` hides warnings
choices.why: It prints them, once per case, in a block that scrolls past.

choices.text: It is free, and the warning shows once
choices.why: Right: easy to read, where forty repeats are easy to skip.

choices.text: Because the first case of a run is never rendered
choices.why: Every case is rendered.

choices.text: Because rendering warms the model's cache for the run
choices.why: Rendering calls no model.

prompt: A placeholder is renamed from `{{tone}}` to `{{register}}`. A script that still passes `tone` now gets a ___, and the run goes ahead.
Why did case `a08` break the structure of `v5-tagged.txt`?

choices.text: The customer typed `</message>`, which closed the tags early
choices.why: Right: the text after it sits outside the message.

choices.text: The message was too long for the tags
choices.why: Length has nothing to do with it.

choices.text: The template has two `<message>` tags
choices.why: The template has one pair; the customer added the rest.

choices.text: Ollama strips tags from the prompt before the model sees them
choices.why: Nothing strips them.

prompt: What does the `|xml` filter change?

choices.text: It removes the customer's tags entirely
choices.why: The text is all still there.

choices.text: It wraps the value in a second pair of tags
choices.why: It adds no tags.

choices.text: It turns `<`, `>` and `&` into entities
choices.why: Right: the customer's tag no longer closes anything.

choices.text: It translates the value into XML
choices.why: It escapes three characters and leaves the rest alone.

prompt: Why is the filter applied to the value and not to the whole template?

choices.text: The template's own tags would be escaped too
choices.why: Right: only text from outside is changed.

choices.text: Filters can only run on short strings
choices.why: There is no such limit.

choices.text: The template has no special characters
choices.why: It has `<message>` and `</message>`.

choices.text: Escaping the template would change its prompt id
choices.why: True, but that is not the reason; its tags would stop being tags.

prompt: Which of these values should be escaped before they are pasted between the template's tags? Choose all that apply.
hint: Where did the text come from?

choices.text: A customer's message
choices.why: Yes: text from outside.

choices.text: A product review pasted from the website
choices.why: Yes: anyone could have written it.

choices.text: The shop's name, chosen by you
choices.why: You chose it; it is part of the instructions.

choices.text: A subject line from an incoming e-mail
choices.why: Yes: a stranger typed it.

prompt: After escaping, `a08` sits whole inside its tags, and the model still gave it `high`, the urgency the customer's text asked for. What follows?

choices.text: Escaping did not work and should be removed
choices.why: It fixed the structure; without it the customer rewrites your prompt.

choices.text: The person's label of `normal` must be wrong
choices.why: Somebody asking where an order is was labelled `normal` on purpose.

choices.text: Escaping is necessary, not sufficient
choices.why: Right: lesson 10 is about the rest.

choices.text: The model only obeys instructions written in capitals, and this one was not
choices.why: The text was not in capitals.

prompt: Why does a test set need one template rendered the same way for every case?
hint: What should a difference between runs mean?

choices.text: So that the runs are shorter
choices.why: Length is not the point.

choices.text: So a difference between runs is the template's
choices.why: Right: forty prompts at once would be noise.

choices.text: So that the model learns the template
choices.why: Nothing is learnt between calls.

choices.text: So that `pl check` can read the replies
choices.why: `pl check` reads replies whatever produced them.

prompt: What is the prompt id that `pl run` prints?

choices.text: A number `pl` gives each run in order
choices.why: Two runs of the same file print the same id.

choices.text: The first eight characters of the SHA-256 of the prompt file
choices.why: Right: `ff210f58` both ways.

choices.text: An id Ollama assigns to the model
choices.why: The model's id is `a80c4f17acd5`, a different thing.

choices.text: A hash of the rendered prompt for the first case
choices.why: It hashes the file, before any rendering.

prompt: Two runs of `v6-escaped.txt` both print `prompt fbc4c9b1`, and one used `--set num_predict=60`. Why is that a problem?

choices.text: Ollama ignored the setting
choices.why: Nothing says it was ignored; the id just does not record it.

choices.text: The run files do not show that they differ
choices.why: Right: a setting on the command line is covered by nothing.

choices.text: The hash function is broken
choices.why: It hashes the file, and the file did not change.

choices.text: The second run overwrote the first
choices.why: They were written to different files.

prompt: A prompt file carries its settings as `name: value` lines above a line of three ___.
Put the steps of putting a changed template to use in order.
items: Render one case and read it

prompt: Match each message from the harness to what it means.

pairs.right: A hole with no value; nothing was sent

pairs.left: `pl: warning: {{tone}} is not in the template`
pairs.right: A value that reached no hole

prompt: Replies that should be in Portuguese started arriving in English yesterday. The template says `Write in {{language}}.`, and your engine renders a missing value as an empty string. What do you check first?
hint: What would the prompt have said?

choices.text: Whether the model was updated yesterday
choices.why: Possible, but the empty-string default is a known way this happens.

choices.text: Whether `language` is still passed under that name
choices.why: Right: a renamed or dropped value renders as *Write in .* with no error.

choices.text: Whether the replies are too long
choices.why: Length does not decide the language.

choices.text: Whether Ollama's default language setting changed
choices.why: Ollama has no default language for replies.
